To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lateral constrictional deformation of hot orogenic lower crust, called Lateral Constrictional Flow, is a widespread phenomenon that is documented in the Neoarchean Dharwar cration of south India and may be a general feature of orogenic plateaux, ultrahot orogenic crusts and inner parts of collision zones.

lateral constrictional flows of the crust are a major process of orogenic plateaux, and that they are driven by gravitational collapse of the upper crust and/or by thrust stacking in the crustal wedge.
lateral constrictional flows in hot lower crust are a common process in orogenic plateaux and that this flow is responsible for the development of the subhorizontal lamination of the lower crust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the lower crust in orogenic settings and the role of lateral constrictional flows in orogenic plateaux.
the role of lateral constrictional strain and flow of hot orogen in the formation of orogenic plateaux and the evolution of orogenic crust.
the dynamics of hot, orogenic crust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LCF, in the case of ultrahot orogenic crust, is the key to the formation and maintenance of large orogenic plateaux.
the lower crust of hot orogens behaves like a hot viscous fluid that is able to flow laterally, to compensate topographic relief, and to mechanically homogenize the crust.
LCF is the most efficient mechanism for orogenic crustal flow, and it may explain the existence of orogenic plateaux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LCF is a major mode of deformation of hot orogens, and its recognition should be a key factor for the understanding of the dynamics of orogenic plateaux and ultrahot orogeny.
the Neoarchean Dharwar cratonic lower crust is a good model for a wide, hot orogen, such as the Neoproterozoic Pan-African belt, the Paleogene Eo-Andean belt, or the present-day Himalayan belt.
the lower crust is not a passive medium, but a major player in the dynamics of hot orogenic plateaux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral flow of the crust is a major mechanism that should be considered in any geodynamic model of orogenic plateaux, collisional crustal wedge, and ultrahot orogeny.
the lower crust is a dynamic and efficient strain and mass redistributor in orogens.
the lower crust can be a key component of orogenic plateaux, and that LCF can be an important mechanism for the formation of orogenic plateaus.
